2. For the purpose of the present petitioner it will be sufficient to notice that the trial Court decreed the suit in part for an amount of tk. 10,57,359.75. Being aggrieved by the said decree plaintiff-petitioner filed F. A. No. 153 of 1987 in the High Court Division. The respondents filed a cross-objection, No. 27 of 1992. By the impugned judgment and order dated 16 January, 1994 a Division Bench, of the High Court Division allowed the appeal and decreed the suit in full. The corss-objection was dismissed. The relevant operative part of the order reads thus: 

 "The defendant-respondents are directed to pay the aforesaid decretal amount within six months from the date of drawing up of the decree in six equal instalments, failing which the plaintiff will be entitled to sell the schedule property and realise the decretal amount with 5/, interest from the date of dues of the aforesaid loan till realisation of the same." 

 3. Petitioner prays for leave to appeal from the impugned judgment and order only on the ground of, as the learned Advocate Mr. Kazi Golam Mahbub submits, refusal of the High Court Division to pass a decree for interest and cost of the suit and the appeal. Mr. Golam Mahbub submits that the petitioner is entitled to interest under the Banking rules and regulations for the capital invested by it and further, to cost of the litigation as the appeal has been allowed in its favour. 

 4. The learned Advocate is perhaps making a confusion as to the claim of interest. Plaintiff has included in the principal sum claimed in the suit the interest also on the money due as on the date of the cause of action i.e. 1.10.1985. The entire amount has already been decreed by the High Court Division. Interest as a substantive claim on principal amount till realization has not been allowed by the trial Court. It does not appear from the impugned judgment or even from the memo of appeal that the petitioner made any specific grievance about it. As to interest under section 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure or as to cost of the suit and appeal plaintiff does not have any statutory right to be paid automatically. The discretion lies with the Court. However, in the instant case the interest has not been altogether denied as will appear from the relevant part of the order quoted above.
